newsitem.title: ABU DHABI: UAE says BAe to have stake in new leasing co.
newsitem.headline: UAE says BAe to have stake in new leasing co.

text.p: British Aerospace (BAe) will take a stake of up to 15 percent in a new leasing company, capitalised at $136 million, which is being set up in the United Arab Emirates, an official UAE statement said on Tuesday.
The statement from The UAE Offsets Group (UOG) confirmed earlier Reuters reports that BAe would put up to $20 million in al-Waha (Oasis) International Leasing Co.

"British Aerospace will be a major investor in the company and its technical partner. Accordingly, British Aerospace will subscribe for up to 15 percent of the shares of the company," the statement said.

It said Oasis would have a 500 million dirham ($136 million) capital, of which 45 percent would be paid in by the founders, with the rest coming from an initial public offering to UAE nationals in June. A total of 50 million shares of 10 dirhams each would be issued.

"Oasis is not an offset project. The participation of British Aerospace in this project was done on an investment basis and not to implement any commitment under the offset programme," UOG vice-president Mohammed al-Mazroui told a news conference.

UAE member Abu Dhabi on Sunday issued a decree setting up the new company which will seek leasing deals in the oil-rich Gulf region for a variety of high-ticket items like commercial aircraft, ships, heavy machinery and power plants.
British Aerospace has provided the Gulf state with military hardware over the years. It is among companies bidding for a UAE requirement for up to 80 warplanes possibly worth more than $6 billion.

Abu Dhabi officials have said they expect the leasing concept to appeal to regional states which are trying to cut capital expenditure as their economies gradually recover from the high costs of the 1991 Gulf War and low oil prices.
